title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). The experiment used a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine). A single shared initial candidate was produced per task by gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performed full intent-constraint and workflow-policy checks and could trigger at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces show repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We incorporate artifact-grounded clarifications of shared-generation semantics, repair-trigger logic, and the statistical degeneracy observed; expand methodological detail, execution accounting, representative diagnostics, and reproducibility guidance; and discuss construct and external validity limits grounded in the archived run artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into network configuration commands, promising efficiency gains for NetOps. However, syntactically plausible commands can violate workflow invariants (for example, changing MTU without an enforced shutdown or performing a hazardous uplink switchover), cause regressions, or otherwise produce semantic failures not visible from text-only checks. Prior proposals therefore recommend integrating verification, emulation, digital twins, or veto layers so generated candidates are validated before enactment. Evaluating these guarded pipelines requires closed-loop executable tests that detect semantic/network-level errors beyond token- or syntax-level correctness.

We designed a preregistered paired experiment to isolate whether an executable validator (and a single-step repair policy) can reduce semantic failures when the same generator output is presented to both a baseline (LLM-only) and a guarded (generate→validate→repair) workflow. Our confirmatory research question (registered as CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) was: Does integrating an executable network emulator as a validator in a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce semantic/network-level failures when enacting LLM-generated configuration changes compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? To isolate validator/repair effects we used a shared-initial-candidate paired design: for each task the same generated candidate was evaluated by both conditions. This isolates the marginal effect of the validator/repair stage on identical generator outputs and avoids conflation with generator variability.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-rich paired experiment (N=120 pairs) that holds the generator fixed and measures the incremental effect of an executable validator plus bounded repair on emulator-observed semantic failures; (2) exact execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation demonstrating completion of the preregistered protocol (planned and completed episodes, model-call counts, contamination checks, and scorer/validator traces); (3) an artifact-grounded analysis and interpretation of a degenerate ceiling outcome (100% success in both conditions), including explicit bootstrap and McNemar reporting; and (4) methodological recommendations for future confirmatory designs when generators produce fewer invalid candidates.
sections.related_work:
Two research strands frame our study. First, NetOps-specific verification and executable-benchmark work emphasize that text-level correctness does not imply safe enactment. Recent executable testbeds and benchmarks (NetConfArena et al.) demonstrate that closed-loop emulation reveals semantic failure modes—sequencing errors, make-before-break mistakes, and group-availability violations—that syntactic checks miss. Second, a growing body of work on tool-augmented LLM agents advocates generate→validate→repair and bounded-autonomy guardrails (veto layers, canaries, translation-to-formal-model) to reduce operational risk. Survey and benchmark reports consistently recommend integrating verification or emulation as a practical safeguard, but empirical cross-model, closed-loop comparisons under identical harnesses remain limited.

Our study complements these efforts by fixing the generator output and experimentally isolating the validator/repair subsystem's marginal effect using an executable emulator. This mechanistic focus differs from prior evaluations that conflate generator variability with verification effects; it therefore offers a different experimental lens on when and how verification/repair components can change operational outcomes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. The study was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) prior to execution. The preregistration specified a paired-binary confirmatory design with exactly N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks, deterministically partitioned into three topology classes (edge/core/leaf–spine) with 40 tasks in each class. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the prespecified test was the exact two-sided McNemar. Complementary reporting included a bootstrap-percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration also defined exclusion and contamination rules, a repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), and deterministic reset controls.

Task generation and payload schema. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest includes structured fields: initial_state, expected_final_state, intent (natural-language intent describing required outcome), required_sequence (the canonical command ordering the validator enforces), and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, difficulty level). The explicit required_sequence allows the emulator validator to check sequencing and workflow policies as structured constraints rather than relying on heuristic textual matching.

Shared-generation design and rationale. For each task we produced a single shared initial candidate using the declared hosted model (gpt-5-mini). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 120 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 120}. The shared-candidate paired design isolates the marginal effect of the validator and repair subsystem by removing generator-induced variability across the paired episodes. This design increases internal validity for the validator effect at the cost of potentially under-exercising repair behavior when the generator already produces valid candidates for the chosen task set.

Validator and repair semantics. The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0), an executable emulator/validator that applies the task-encoded workflow policies (for example: must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break patterns). The validator executes the candidate in an emulated final-state checker and emits a structured validator_trace including validation_before, validation_after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, and repair_applied. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair iteration and invoked a repair prompt only when validator.violation_count>0. Repair artifacts (repair_prompt_trace, repair_provider_trace) are archived when generated; in this run they were not generated because no violations were detected.

Instrumentation, contamination controls, and deterministic reconciliation. The harness enforced deterministic emulator resets between tasks (container image checksums + deterministic seeds) and recorded provider-call audits. Contamination heuristics (duplicate-output detection, cross-condition cache-key reuse) were applied and recorded; none triggered exclusions. The final deterministic_reconciliation artifact confirms complete accounting (planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; complete_pair_count = 120; hosted_model_call_event_count = 120; cross-condition cache reuse = false). All instrumentation and audit logs used in analysis are archived and checksummed in the execution manifest.

Statistical analysis details and degenerate-interval clarification. The preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar applied to binary pass/fail labels per pair. The bootstrap-percentile CI was computed by resampling paired outcomes (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and recording the paired-difference distribution. When the empirical contingency table contains zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0), every bootstrap resample reproduces an identical paired table and produces the same paired-difference (0.00). Consequently the percentile interval is degenerate (lower = upper = 0.00). This degenerate CI is an exact consequence of the observed concordant data and the resampling method specified in the preregistration, not an implementation fault.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcome. The preregistered run completed without technical exclusions: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). Condition-level summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) record baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0, guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table records n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0 and the paired-difference estimate = 0.00. The preregistered bootstrap-percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) returned [0.00, 0.00]; the CI is degenerate because there are no discordant pairs to produce sampling variability in the paired-difference estimator.

Per-topology breakdown. The deterministic task partition produced 40 tasks per topology class. Per-topology outcomes are:
- Edge (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
- Core (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
- Leaf–spine (40 tasks): baseline = 40/40 success; guarded = 40/40 success.
These per-topology counts are recorded in the archived task manifest and reproduced in the scoring JSON artifacts. The uniform per-topology success confirms the ceiling outcome occurred across the curated difficulty strata represented in the manifest.

Representative validator diagnostics. Representative scoring artifacts (for example, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json) show the same pattern: normalized_response equals normalized_reference_answer; parsed_command_count equals required_command_count from the task payload; validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true; validator_trace.repair_applied = false; validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; validator_version = 5.0. Example task payloads include explicit required_sequence entries (shut→configure→restore, make-before-break, dual-down MTU change) that the validator enforces as structured checks; the archived traces show these canonical constraints were satisfied by the generator output under the frozen prompting strategy.

Repair activity and secondary endpoints. Because validator.violation_count = 0 for every guarded episode, repair_applied = false across the run and no repair_provider_trace artifacts exist. Consequently, preregistered secondary endpoints that quantify repair incidence and repair-call counts are vacuous in this run and are reported as such in the archived analysis artifacts. The absence of repair activity is itself an empirical observation grounded in the validator traces.

Contamination, missingness, and reconciliation. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty and analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 120 with zero technical/instrumentation exclusions. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact confirms all provider-audit counts and pair accounting are internally consistent (n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0; hosted_model_call_event_count = 120). These reconciliations support the integrity of the confirmatory statistics reported above.

Compact execution metadata table. Table 2 (see captions) summarizes key execution metadata drawn verbatim from archived artifacts: planned vs completed episodes, model_calls_used, validator identifier/version, task-count by topology class, and bootstrap parameters (resamples and seed). These exact numbers are available in the execution and analysis artifact files referenced in the preregistration and execution manifests.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the ceiling outcome. The shared-generation paired design was intended to answer a narrowly scoped mechanistic question: can a validator/repair subsystem improve outcomes for identical generator outputs? In this archived task bank and under the declared generator/prompt configuration the shared initial candidates satisfied the deterministic emulator validator in all 120 pairs; consequently the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to exercise repair behavior and could not reduce semantic failures relative to the baseline. The observed exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrapped CI = [0.00, 0.00] are statistical expressions of this ceiling.

Design trade-offs and recommendations. The shared-generation protocol increases internal validity for isolating validator effects but can under-exercise repair when the generator is already well-calibrated for the curated task bank. Based on the archived manifest fields (difficulty metadata: dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, difficulty level) we recommend three pragmatic confirmatory design adjustments for future runs that aim to demonstrate repair utility: (1) independent generation per condition so the guard can intercept generator errors arising from prompt or sampling variability; (2) controlled prompt perturbations (the preregistration included exploratory prompt-perturbation plans) applied to a subset of tasks to increase generator error incidence while preserving paired blocking for other controls; (3) stratified selection of tasks with higher dependency_rule_count or 'very_hard' difficulty tags from the task manifest to concentrate on task families that historically produce generator mistakes.

Operational implications. Even when unused, a deterministic validator that emits structured traces (which rules were checked, which fields were touched, and why a repair was not applied) supports operator auditability and post-hoc analysis. The archived artifacts demonstrate end-to-end instrumented accounting (provider-call audits, scoring traces, deterministic reconciliation) that can be repurposed for operator-facing explanations and third-party audits in production deployments where generators sometimes err. The experiment also underscores that claims about repair benefits require careful experimental framing: if generators rarely produce invalid candidates under a chosen prompt, the guard will be idle by design.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: robust—deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audit logs, zero exclusions, and reproducible validator traces. Construct validity: limited by the validator's policy encodings derived from synthetic task payloads; the validator enforces a specific, explicit set of workflow policies that may not capture vendor heterogeneity or timing/telemetry constraints encountered in production. External validity: constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈0.40 and targeted absolute reduction 0.15; with baseline observed = 0.00 those assumptions do not hold and the confirmatory test is uninformative for demonstrating the originally targeted effect size.

Reproducibility and artifact utility. All primary and secondary execution artifacts required to reproduce the reported accounting are archived and checksummed in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts (representative artifacts listed in the Disclosure Statement). The execution manifest records stage accounting (shared_initial_generation = 120), and the analysis artifacts include paired_contingency_table.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json which together allow independent verification of the confirmatory contingency counts and provider-call audits. Researchers wishing to explore guard exercise strategies can reuse the archived task_manifest difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) to construct targeted follow-ups without changing the underlying harness semantics.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, producing n_11 = 120 (both conditions success) and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The result documents a ceiling on this curated synthetic task bank and clarifies that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear if generators sometimes produce invalid candidates. Our principal scientific contribution is methodological: we demonstrate how a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects and how deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the primary confirmatory test is degenerate. The archived artifacts permit follow-up studies that relax the shared-generation constraint, compare generator families, expand repair budgets, and evaluate more production-rooted corpora to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
